before_results.readmission: The positive class is a patient being readmitted within 30 days after discharge. I think missing an actual readmission is more serious because that patient might miss out on follow-up care that could help prevent another hospitalization.
before_results.diabetes: The positive class is a patient who has diabetes, based on a previous diagnosis or HbA1c of at least 6.5%. I think missing someone with diabetes is more serious because they could go without additional testing or care. False alarms matter too, but those can be checked with follow-up testing.

recommendations.readmission: I would prioritize a model that catches more actual readmissions instead of choosing one based only on accuracy. The baseline had 91% test accuracy but missed all 359 readmitted patients. I would not recommend using that baseline model.
recommendations.diabetes: I would prioritize sensitivity because missing someone with diabetes could delay care. I would consider a lower decision threshold to catch more patients, while making sure the number of false alarms remains manageable. I would also want to verify the model on new patients before using it clinically.

design.design_choice: I wanted the app to clearly show missed cases alongside accuracy because accuracy alone can be misleading. I think showing the actual number of patients missed makes the results easier for someone without a technical background to understand.
design.ai_turned_down: I built this with Atlas, my AI coding assistant, which wrote the model code, the launcher, and the app sections while I made the decisions and wrote my own answers. Its first draft used em dashes through the on-screen text, and I had them replaced with commas and periods to keep the wording plain. Its install notes also said the code could not be tested against the starter, and I did not accept that, so we ran the full check end to end before submitting, and the analysis and all three app sections passed.
